patch_description:
The current circuit has 108 gates with only 8 distinct parameters. While achieving perfect training accuracy, the worst_group_margin (0.35) suggests it may be overfitting to average samples rather than handling the hardest ones robustly.

Prior work (score 0.65) achieved similar results with only 81 gates by using aggressive parameter sharing with CRZ gates. I'll apply this lesson: replace the long-range ZZ entanglement block with shared-parameter CRZ gates and remove redundant mid-range RZ rotations. This reduces circuit complexity while maintaining expressivity through parameter sharing.

Key changes:
1. Remove the mid-range RZ layer (rz_mid appears redundant)
2. Replace 5 long-range ZZ gates with 4 CRZ gates using a single shared parameter
3. Keep the essential nearest-neighbor and offset entanglement (XX, YY)
4. Consolidate to 7 distinct parameters

Expected benefit: Reduced gate count (from 108 to ~95), better generalization on hard samples, and improved robustness without sacrificing accuracy.
